errors.text_span: The chart is divided into ten slices
errors.evidence: The description states ten slices, but then lists 14 categories. Looking at the figure, there are more than 10 distinct segments visible (including Content Analysis, Semantic Layer subcategories, Perception Layer subcategories, Cultural Layer subcategories, Signal Layer, etc.).

errors.text_span: The slices are colored in varying shades of blue and pink
errors.evidence: The chart uses varying shades of blue and gray/silver, not pink. No pink color is visible in the figure.

errors.text_span: Some slices have percentage labels directly within the segment; the "Cultural Layer" slice is labeled as 14.1%, the "Semantic Layer" is labeled as 41.2%, and the "Signal Layer" is labeled as 4.3%. The "Perception Layer" represents the largest section of the pie chart, at approximately 40.4%.
errors.evidence: The chart is a donut/sunburst chart with an inner ring showing layers (Signal Layer 4.3%, Cultural Layer 14.1%, Semantic Layer 41.2%, Perception Layer 40.4%) and an outer ring showing subcategories. The description mixes up the structural levels and incorrectly describes this as a simple pie chart with some percentage labels.

The chart is a sunburst/donut chart with two concentric rings (an inner ring showing four main layers with percentages and an outer ring showing subcategories). The description does not mention this nested/hierarchical structure, which is a fundamental visual feature of the chart.

The description does not mention that the outer ring shows task subcategories belonging to each of the four main layers (Content Analysis, Perception Layer, Cultural Layer, Signal Layer), which is essential to understanding the chart's purpose.
No legend is visible in the figure. The chart uses direct labels on the segments.
The description does not mention the 'Content Analysis' label visible in the outer ring, which is one of the main categories.

errors.text_span: The segments are visually ordered with generally larger segments appearing towards the right side of the chart, and smaller segments towards the left.
errors.evidence: This is an oversimplification. The Perception Layer (40.4%) is on the left/bottom, and the Semantic Layer (41.2%) is on the right, so the large segments are distributed across the chart, not predominantly on the right.
